import numpy as np

N = 20
k = 9
# Construction based on a circulant graph: v -> v+s (mod N) where s is in S.
# We choose S = {1, 2, ..., 9}
S = list(range(1, k + 1))

# Build the adjacency matrix for the conflict graph H (undirected).
# H[i, j] = True if i and j are connected in G (i -> j or j -> i).
H = np.zeros((N, N), dtype=bool)

for i in range(N):
    for j in range(N):
        if i == j:
            continue
        
        # Check if i knows j (i -> j)
        # Edge exists if j - i is in S (mod N)
        diff_ij = (j - i) % N
        i_knows_j = diff_ij in S
        
        # Check if j knows i (j -> i)
        # Edge exists if i - j is in S (mod N)
        diff_ji = (i - j) % N
        j_knows_i = diff_ji in S
        
        # They are connected in H if there is knowledge in either direction
        H[i, j] = i_knows_j or j_knows_i

# The problem is finding the chromatic number of H, chi(H).
# We use the lower bound based on the maximum independent set size alpha(H): chi(H) >= N / alpha(H).

def find_max_independent_set_size(adj_matrix):
    # For small N, we can try checking possible sizes, but for a general bound, 
    # we rely on structural properties. Since this specific construction leads to 
    # a known structure (related to difference graphs/Paley graphs), we check the 
    # maximum possible size based on the definition of independence.
    
    N = adj_matrix.shape[0]
    
    # An independent set I is a set where for any u, v in I, 
    # the difference |u - v| (mod N) is not in S U (-S).
    # S = {1, ..., 9}. -S = {11, ..., 19} (mod 20).
    # S U (-S) = {1, 2, ..., 9, 11, 12, ..., 19}.
    # The only difference not in this set is 10.
    
    # Therefore, an independent set I can only contain vertices u, v 
    # if u - v = 10 (mod 20).
    # This means I can be a subset of {0, 10} or {1, 11} or {2, 12}, etc.
    # The maximum size is 2.
    return 2

alpha_H = find_max_independent_set_size(H)
chromatic_lower_bound = N / alpha_H

print(f"N: {N}")
print(f"Maximum Independent Set Size alpha(H): {alpha_H}")
print(f"Chromatic Lower Bound (N/alpha(H)): {chromatic_lower_bound}")

# Also check the degree (Delta) as an upper bound reference
degrees = np.sum(H, axis=1)
delta_H = np.max(degrees)
print(f"Maximum Degree Delta(H): {delta_H}")
